Na prvé sedenie stačí chuť hrať, pár kociek a niekto, kto hru povedie. Táto kniha ťa prevedie piatimi kapitolami od prázdneho stola po prvé dobrodružstvo. Nájdi skupinu Ideálne sú 3 až 5 hráči a jeden Dungeon Master. Skús kamarátov, klub v okolí, obchod so spoločenskými hrami alebo online skupinu. Vytvor si postavu Vyber rasu (človek, elf, trpaslík…) a povolanie (bojovník, mág, zlodej…). Na prvú hru ti DM často dá hotovú postavu. Vyskúšaj tvorbu postavy Zožeň kocky Klasická sada má sedem kociek. Kým si ju kúpiš, poslúži náš hádzač v menu Kocky. Pochop základný hod Keď sa postava pokúsi o niečo, čo môže zlyhať, hodíš d20 a pripočítaš jej bonus. Ak je výsledok rovnaký alebo vyšší ako obtiažnosť (DC), ktorú určí DM, podarilo sa. Preskočiť priepasť: d20 (13) + Atletika 3 = 16 · DC 15 · úspech Zahraj si krátke dobrodružstvo Jednorazová hra (one-shot) na 3 až 4 hodiny je najlepší prvý krok. Základné pravidlá piatej edície sú voľne dostupné ako SRD 5.2. Vygeneruj si zápletku Knižnica Povolania Všetkých 12 povolaní, ich úloha v družine a ktoré sú vhodné na začiatok. Here are all twelve fifth edition classes and what to expect from each. Barbarian Bard Cleric Druid Fighter Monk Paladin Ranger Rogue Sorcerer Warlock Wizard Can't decide? For a first game the fighter, barbarian, rogue and paladin are the easiest. Front-line brawler d12 Barbarian Barbarians draw power from rage. While raging they hit harder and shrug off half the damage from weapons. They have more hit points than any other class, so they can take what would drop anyone else. Primary ability: Strength Saving throws: Strength , Constitution Hit die: d12 Complexity: ●○○ beginner friendly Pick it if you want to be on the front line without tracking spells. Support caster d8 Bard Bards weave magic from music, words and stories. They spur allies on with Bardic Inspiration, cast spells that heal or confuse, and can talk their way out of most trouble. Primary ability: Charisma Saving throws: Dexterity , Charisma Hit die: d8 Complexity: ●●○ moderate Pick it if you love speaking in character and helping the whole party. Healer and protector d8 Cleric Clerics receive their spells from a deity. They heal, shield and bolster allies, yet with armour and a shield they hold their own in melee. With divine power they can turn the undead. Primary ability: Wisdom Saving throws: Wisdom , Charisma Hit die: d8 Complexity: ●●○ moderate Pick it if you want to keep the party alive without standing aside when the fighting starts. Nature caster d8 Druid Druids draw magic from nature itself. They call down lightning and grasping vines, heal, and can take the shape of a beast, from a wolf to a bear. Primary ability: Wisdom Saving throws: Intelligence , Wisdom Hit die: d8 Complexity: ●●● for experienced players Pick it if the wild calls to you and you want a different trick up your sleeve every time. Weapon master d10 Fighter Fighters master every weapon and every kind of armour. Second Wind restores hit points mid-fight, and Action Surge lets them do twice as much in a single turn. The most forgiving pick for a first game. Primary ability: Strength or Dexterity Saving throws: Strength , Constitution Hit die: d10 Complexity: ●○○ beginner friendly Pick it if you want a simple but strong character and would rather learn the rules as you go. Swift unarmed fighter d8 Monk Monks fight with fists and feet, honed by years of discipline. They move faster than anyone, strike several times a turn and use inner focus to dodge blows and blasts alike. Primary ability: Dexterity and Wisdom Saving throws: Strength , Dexterity Hit die: d8 Complexity: ●●○ moderate Pick it if you enjoy a mobile fighting style without weapons or armour. Holy knight d10 Paladin Paladins are knights bound by a sacred oath. They wear heavy armour, heal wounds with a touch and can charge a weapon hit with divine power for a devastating smite. Primary ability: Strength and Charisma Saving throws: Wisdom , Charisma Hit die: d10 Complexity: ●○○ beginner friendly Pick it if you want to fight on the front line with a little magic on the side. Tracker and archer d10 Ranger Rangers are at home in the wild. They track, survive anywhere, are deadly with a bow and lean on nature magic such as Hunter's Mark to strike their quarry harder. Primary ability: Dexterity and Wisdom Saving throws: Strength , Dexterity Hit die: d10 Complexity: ●●○ moderate Pick it if you want to shoot from range and be the eyes and ears of the party. Sneak and specialist d8 Rogue Rogues rely on skill, not brute force. They pick locks, disarm traps and land a Sneak Attack where it hurts most. Cunning Action lets them hide or slip away every single turn. Primary ability: Dexterity Saving throws: Dexterity , Intelligence Hit die: d8 Complexity: ●○○ beginner friendly Pick it if you like working out how to get where you shouldn't be. Innate caster d6 Sorcerer Sorcerers are born with magic in their blood. They know fewer spells than a wizard, but bend them with Metamagic: twinning them onto two targets, empowering them or casting them silently. Primary ability: Charisma Saving throws: Constitution , Charisma Hit die: d6 Complexity: ●●● for experienced players Pick it if you want big spells and a personal story about where your power came from. Pact caster d8 Warlock Warlocks have struck a pact with a powerful patron: a fey lord, a fiend or something older still. They have few spell slots but regain them on a short rest, and their Eldritch Blast is one of the best cantrips in the game. Primary ability: Charisma Saving throws: Wisdom , Charisma Hit die: d8 Complexity: ●●○ moderate Pick it if you are drawn to a dark secret and a bargain that comes at a price. Scholar of magic d6 Wizard Wizards learn spells through study and record them in a spellbook. They have the widest choice of spells of any class but are fragile, so they need to think about where they stand in a fight. Primary ability: Intelligence Saving throws: Intelligence , Wisdom Hit die: d6 Complexity: ●●● for experienced players Pick it if you like planning ahead and want an answer to every problem. Here are the most common terms explained simply, so you can follow both the rulebook and the table talk. 5e fifth edition The current version of the DnD rules, played by most groups today. The revised rules came out in 2024. Ability check A d20 plus a modifier when a character attempts something uncertain, such as climbing a wall or talking past a guard. Ability scores Six numbers that describe a character: Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma. They usually range from 8 to 20. Action, bonus action, reaction On its turn a character has one action (attack, spell, dash) and sometimes a bonus action. A reaction can be used once a round, even outside its turn. Advantage and disadvantage Roll two d20s. Take the higher with advantage, the lower with disadvantage. Armor Class AC How hard a character is to hit. An attack hits if the attack roll meets or beats it. Campaign and one-shot A campaign is a long story over many sessions. A one-shot is a single-evening adventure. Cantrip A simple spell that uses no spell slot, so it can be cast at will. Character sheet The sheet where a player records everything about their character: abilities, hit points, gear and spells. Concentration Some spells last only while the caster concentrates. They can hold just one at a time, and taking damage can break it. Critical hit natural 20 The d20 shows a 20 on an attack. The attack always hits and the damage dice are rolled twice. d20 die The twenty-sided die, the most important die in the game. "d" means die and the number is its sides, so 2d6 is two six-sided dice. DC Difficulty Class How hard a task is, set by the DM. Easy is around 10, hard is 20. The roll must meet or beat it. Death saving throws A character at zero hit points rolls a d20 each turn. Three successes (10 or higher) stabilise them, three failures mean death. DM Dungeon Master The game's narrator and referee. Describes the world, plays every character except the players' own and makes the call when the rules run out. Heroic Inspiration A reward from the DM for great play, or a feature of some characters. It lets you reroll one die. Hit Dice A die set by the class (d6 to d12). It decides how many hit points a character gains each level, and is spent to heal on a short rest. Hit points HP How much damage a character can take. At zero they fall unconscious and start making death saving throws. Homebrew house content Rules, monsters or worlds a group or DM made up themselves, outside the official books. Initiative A roll at the start of combat that sets the order in which characters and monsters take turns. Level and experience XP Characters start at 1st level and earn experience for overcoming challenges. Each level brings more hit points and new abilities, up to 20th. Metagaming When a player has their character act on knowledge only the player has, such as a monster's stats from the book. Modifier The bonus or penalty that comes from an ability score. A score of 10 gives +0, and every two points above it add +1. It is added to rolls. Multiclassing An optional rule that lets a character take a level in a different class when they level up. Natural 1 The d20 shows a 1 on an attack. The attack misses, whatever the bonuses. NPC non-player character A character played by the DM: the innkeeper, the king, the dragon and the passer-by. Party The group of player characters who travel together and face adventures side by side. Player character PC A hero played by one of the players. Every other character in the world is an NPC. Proficiency bonus A bonus for what a character is trained in: weapons, skills and tools. It starts at +2 and grows with level. Saving throw A roll to resist something happening to a character: poison, a trap, a fireball. Every class is proficient in two. Session zero A meeting before a campaign starts where the group agrees on tone and boundaries and makes characters together. Short and long rest A short rest takes an hour and restores some abilities. A long rest takes eight hours and restores all hit points and spell slots. Skill An area a character can be proficient in, such as Athletics, Stealth or Persuasion. Proficiency adds its bonus to the check. Spell slot A store of magical energy. Every spell of 1st level or higher uses one, and rest restores them. SRD System Reference Document The free core rules of the fifth edition under a Creative Commons licence. They are enough to play. Subclass A specialisation within a class, chosen at 3rd level, such as the Champion fighter or the Illusionist wizard. TTRPG tabletop role-playing game The genre DnD belongs to.
